docs.title: ADR Status Board — DVT+ (Extensive Governance Version)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-02-21

This document tracks the maturity level of architectural decisions and defines concrete evidence required to transition each ADR to Accepted.

docs.title: ADR-0010 — Run Event Envelope Split
docs.text:
Status: Pending Implementation

Completion requires:

  • IdempotencyKeyBuilder implemented
  • Canonicalization formally tested
  • Store append atomicity verified
  • Outbox processes appended only
  • runSeq strictly monotonic per runId
  • Replay test suite passes

Architectural Impact: High — foundational to event correctness

docs.title: ADR-0011 — RunStarted Ownership
docs.text:
Status: Proposed

Needs verification that:

  • Engine emits RunQueued only
  • Adapter/workflow emits RunStarted
  • Ordering preserved via runSeq
  • No duplication on retries

If implementation matches ADR → mark Accepted.

docs.title: ADR-0012 — Plan Integrity Ownership
docs.text:
Status: Pending Implementation

To close:

  • Engine no longer fetches plan bytes
  • Adapter validates bytes-level integrity
  • Shared plan-verifier exists
  • Contract tests cover hash mismatch & schema failure

Architectural Impact: High — execution trust boundary

docs.title: ADR-0012a — Canonical Error Code Strategy
docs.text:
Status: Proposed

Next:

  • Introduce PlanErrorCode enum in @dvt/contracts
  • Map adapter-specific errors
  • Contract test canonical emission
  • Deprecation window defined

Impact: Medium — observability consistency

docs.title: ADR-0013 — bootstrapRunTx
docs.text:
Status: Proposed

Confirm:

  • Transactional append + enqueue atomic
  • Outbox behavior verified
  • Integration test covers crash recovery

Impact: High — durability & correctness

docs.title: Governance Principle
docs.text:
An ADR moves to Accepted only when:

  1. Code matches normative specification.
  2. Tests prove invariants.
  3. No known contradictions remain.
  4. Evidence links are documented in the ADR.

This prevents “paper architecture” divergence.

Reference:

  • Architecture Decision Records (ADR methodology) https://adr.github.io/

docs.title: Roadmap de Implementación — Basado en Revisión Arquitectónica
docs.text:
Fecha: 2026-02-21 Fuente: Revisión arquitectónica profunda contra ADR-0003 a ADR-0016, contratos normativos v2.0.x, e implementación actual de WorkflowEngine.ts / IProviderAdapter.ts

Este documento complementa ROADMAP.md. No reemplaza las fases existentes; las extiende con tareas concretas derivadas de las discrepancias encontradas entre código, ADRs y contratos normativos.

Criterio de priorización:

  • WAVE 0 — Bugs activos. Código incorrecto hoy. Bloquean correctness garantizada antes de cualquier merge a producción.
  • WAVE 1 — Reconciliación de contratos. Documentos contradictorios que generarán implementaciones incorrectas si no se resuelven.
  • WAVE 2 — Critical path abierto. Issues existentes bloqueados o con dependencias no resueltas.
  • WAVE 3 — Fundamentos operacionales. Sin esto, la fase 1.5 falla.
  • WAVE 4 — Hardening (alineado con Phase 1.5 del ROADMAP.md existente).
  • WAVE 5 — Expansión de plataforma (alineado con Phase 2+).

docs.title: WAVE 0 — Bugs Activos (Bloquean correctness)
docs.text: Estas tareas describen código que produce comportamiento incorrecto hoy. Ningún merge a main que dependa de WorkflowEngine debe quedar abierto mientras estas tareas existan.

docs.title: W0-1 — Eliminar IPlanFetcher del WorkflowEngine
docs.text:
Problema: WorkflowEngine.startRun llama this.deps.planFetcher.fetch(validatedPlanRef) en la línea 146. ADR-0012 §4 dice: "Engine MUST NOT fetch plan bytes." El ADR fue escrito para corregir exactamente esto. No fue implementado.

Tarea:

  • Eliminar IPlanFetcher de WorkflowEngineDeps.
  • Eliminar la llamada planFetcher.fetch() de startRun.
  • El engine pasa planRef (no plan) al adapter directamente.
  • Eliminar el import y la dependencia de IPlanFetcher en WorkflowEngine.ts.

Criterio de aceptación:

  • WorkflowEngine no importa ni instancia IPlanFetcher.
  • startRun pasa validatedPlanRef al adapter, no un ExecutionPlan resuelto.
  • Tests de unidad de WorkflowEngine no mockean planFetcher.
  • tsc --noEmit pasa.

Archivos afectados:

  • WorkflowEngine.ts
  • IPlanFetcher.ts — candidato a eliminación

Dependencia: W0-2 debe completarse simultáneamente (cambio de firma del adapter).

docs.title: W0-2 — Cambiar firma de IProviderAdapter.startRun: ExecutionPlan → PlanRef
docs.text:
Problema: IProviderAdapter.startRun(plan: ExecutionPlan, ...) recibe el plan ya resuelto. Tres documentos contradicen esto:

  • IWorkflowEngine.v2.0.md §2: "startRun MUST accept PlanRef"
  • ADR-0014: "adapter.startRun(planRef, context)"
  • ADR-0012 §4: "Adapters MUST: 1. Fetch bytes from PlanRef.uri; 2. Verify sha256"

Tarea:

  • Cambiar IProviderAdapter.startRun(plan: ExecutionPlan, ctx) a startRun(planRef: PlanRef, ctx).
  • Actualizar MockAdapter, TemporalAdapterStub, ConductorAdapterStub con la nueva firma.
  • El adapter (no el engine) es responsable de fetch + verificación de integridad.

Criterio de aceptación:

  • IProviderAdapter.startRun recibe PlanRef, no ExecutionPlan.
  • WorkflowEngine pasa validatedPlanRef al adapter.
  • MockAdapter implementa fetch interno (puede ser in-memory/noop para tests).
  • Todos los stubs compilados y con tipo correcto.

Archivos afectados:

  • IProviderAdapter.ts
  • MockAdapter.ts
  • TemporalAdapterStub.ts
  • ConductorAdapterStub.ts

Dependencia: W0-1 (simultáneos), W0-3 (el verifier es el que se inyecta en el adapter).

docs.title: W0-3 — Crear @dvt/plan-verifier
docs.text:
Problema: ADR-0012 §6 manda: "All adapters MUST use @dvt/plan-verifier." No existe. Sin él, cada adapter implementará su propia verificación SHA-256 y se desalinearán.

Tarea: Crear packages/@dvt/plan-verifier/ con:

src/
  verifyPlanIntegrity.ts   — fetch bytes, sha256(bytes) === PlanRef.sha256, lanza PlanErrorCode
  parsePlan.ts             — parse + validación de schema (zod)
  verifyPlanIdentity.ts    — planId/version/tenantId match
  errors.ts                — enum PlanErrorCode (HASH_MISMATCH | SCHEMA_INVALID | IDENTITY_MISMATCH | FETCH_FAILED)
  index.ts

Criterio de aceptación:

  • verifyPlanIntegrity(planRef, fetchFn) retorna ExecutionPlan o lanza PlanVerificationError con PlanErrorCode.
  • Hash se computa sobre bytes crudos, no sobre JSON re-serializado.
  • MockAdapter y TemporalAdapterStub usan el paquete.
  • Tests de contrato: hash mismatch → HASH_MISMATCH; schema inválido → SCHEMA_INVALID; id mismatch → IDENTITY_MISMATCH.

docs.title: W0-4 — Eliminar la ventana entre bootstrapRunTx y saveProviderRef
docs.text:
Problema: En startRun hay una escritura en dos fases:

  1. bootstrapRunTx(...) — persiste con providerWorkflowId: '' y providerRunId: ''
  2. adapter.startRun(...) — retorna el EngineRunRef
  3. saveProviderRef(...) — segunda escritura que rellena los IDs

Si el proceso muere después del paso 2, el run está activo en el provider pero el state store tiene IDs vacíos. cancelRun y getRunStatus no pueden alcanzar al provider.

Tarea:

  • bootstrapRunTx debe incluir providerWorkflowId y providerRunId en la metadata inicial.
  • Esto requiere que adapter.startRun se llame antes de bootstrapRunTx, o bien que el adapter retorne el ref como parte de una confirmación atómica.
  • Opción recomendada: llamar adapter.startRun primero → obtener runRef → llamar bootstrapRunTx con el ref incluido. Si bootstrapRunTx falla, llamar adapter.cancelRun como compensación.
  • Eliminar saveProviderRef del IRunStateStore.

Criterio de aceptación:

  • No existe llamada a saveProviderRef en WorkflowEngine.startRun.
  • RunMetadata tras bootstrapRunTx siempre tiene providerWorkflowId y providerRunId no vacíos.
  • Test: simular fallo de bootstrapRunTx después de adapter.startRun → verificar que se emite cancelación compensatoria.
  • buildRunMetadata no inicializa strings vacíos para campos de provider.

Archivos afectados:

  • WorkflowEngine.ts — startRun, saveProviderRef, buildRunMetadata
  • IRunStateStore.ts — eliminar saveProviderRef

docs.title: W0-5 — Corregir idempotency key de señales (signalKey)
docs.text:
Problema: IdempotencyKeyBuilder.signalKey produce:

['sig', tenantId, runId, req.signalId].join('|');
  • No es SHA-256. Formato incompatible con los lifecycle events.
  • Incluye tenantId, que el contrato normativo prohíbe en la derivación.
  • No está definido en ningún contrato normativo.

Tarea:

  • Definir la fórmula de idempotencia para señales en RunEvents.v2.0.md o en SignalsAndAuth v1.1 (documentar la dependencia).
  • Fórmula propuesta: SHA256(runId | 'SIGNAL' | signalType | signalId | logicalAttemptId | planId | planVersion).
  • Actualizar signalKey() en IdempotencyKeyBuilder para seguir la fórmula.
  • Agregar golden test vectors para señales.

Criterio de aceptación:

  • signalKey() retorna un SHA-256 hex string.
  • La fórmula está documentada en el contrato normativo correspondiente.
  • Golden vectors incluidos en el contrato.
  • Tests de contrato validan la derivación.

Archivos afectados:

  • idempotency.ts
  • docs/architecture/engine/contracts/engine/RunEvents.v2.0.md o nuevo contrato de señales

docs.title: W0-6 — Separar enriquecimiento del provider de getRunStatus (ADR-0015)
docs.text:
Problema: WorkflowEngine.getRunStatus llama adapter.getRunStatus() síncronamente con timeout de 30s. ADR-0015: "The default read path MUST NOT call the provider." En una instalación multi-réplica, el circuit breaker in-process no protege nada.

Tarea:

  • En WorkflowEngine.getRunStatus: eliminar el bloque if (adapter) { const providerView = await ... } del path principal.
  • Crear método separado enrichRunStatus(engineRunRef) que llama al provider y puede fallar sin afectar el estado autoritativo.
  • Eliminar circuitStateByProvider del WorkflowEngine (el circuit breaker in-process es inútil en multi-réplica; si hay un circuit breaker real, debe vivir en infraestructura externa).

Criterio de aceptación:

  • getRunStatus retorna el estado proyectado del event log solamente.
  • Latencia de getRunStatus no depende de la disponibilidad del provider.
  • enrichRunStatus existe como método separado (o endpoint separado en la API).
  • circuitStateByProvider eliminado o movido a enrichRunStatus.
  • Tests de unidad: getRunStatus no mockea adapter.getRunStatus.

Archivos afectados:

  • WorkflowEngine.ts — getRunStatus, withCircuitBreaker

docs.title: W0-7 — Snapshot write-through en appendAndEnqueueTx
docs.text:
Problema: getRunStatus usa un snapshot almacenado, pero no existe ningún mecanismo que actualice el snapshot después de cada append. Flujo actual:

  1. Evento se append → snapshot no se actualiza
  2. getRunStatus → lee snapshot stale → llama listEvents (full replay O(n)) si no hay snapshot

Tarea:

  • Tras cada appendAndEnqueueTx exitoso, applyRunEvent debe aplicarse al snapshot actual y upsertarlo.
  • Esto puede hacerse en la capa del IRunStateStore (el store actualiza snapshot como parte de la transacción) o en el caller.
  • La función applyRunEvent ya es pura y exportada — úsala directamente en la lógica de append.
  • Agregar upsertSnapshot(snapshot: WorkflowSnapshot): Promise<void> a IRunStateStore si no existe.

Criterio de aceptación:

  • Después de cada append, el snapshot del run refleja el nuevo estado.
  • getRunStatus nunca llama listEvents para runs activos (solo para runs pre-snapshot que son legacy).
  • Test: append 10 eventos → getSnapshot retorna snapshot con todos los estados aplicados sin full replay.

docs.title: WAVE 1 — Reconciliación de Contratos
docs.text: Documentos contradictorios que generarán bugs silenciosos en nuevas implementaciones si no se resuelven ahora.

docs.title: W1-1 — Deprecar sección de idempotencia de ADR-0010
docs.text:
Problema: ADR-0010 §4 incluye payload en la derivación del idempotencyKey (referencia RFC 8785). RunEvents.v2.0.1 §3.1 excluye payload explícitamente y define exactamente 6 campos. La implementación sigue v2.0.1 (correcto), pero ADR-0010 sigue siendo el documento "Approved".

Tarea:

  • Agregar una nota en ADR-0010 §4: "SUPERSEDED BY RunEvents.v2.0.1 §3.1. La fórmula definitiva excluye payload. Este ADR no debe usarse como referencia para derivación de idempotencyKey."
  • Actualizar el status de ADR-0010 a Accepted (partial — §4 superseded).
  • Agregar referencia cruzada en RunEvents.v2.0.1 apuntando a la obsolescencia de ADR-0010 §4.

Criterio de aceptación:

  • ADR-0010 anotado. Ningún implementador puede leer §4 sin ver la advertencia de superseded.
  • La sección de idempotencia de ADR-0010 tiene un bloqueo visual claro (> ⚠️ SUPERSEDED).

docs.title: W1-2 — Actualizar IRunStateStore.v2.0.md para reflejar la implementación real
docs.text:
Problema: El contrato normativo v2.0.0 define:

interface IRunStateStore {
  appendEvent(event: RunEventWrite): Promise<AppendResult>;
  fetchEvents(runId, options?): Promise<RunEventRecord[]>;
  getSnapshot(runId): Promise<RunSnapshot | null>;
  projectSnapshot(runId): Promise<RunSnapshot>;
}

La implementación real tiene: bootstrapRunTx, appendAndEnqueueTx, getRunMetadataByRunId, saveProviderRef, listEvents, listRuns, getSnapshot. Son interfaces completamente distintas. El contrato normativo está desactualizado.

Tarea:

  • Actualizar IRunStateStore.v2.0.md a v2.1.0 (minor bump — backwards incompatible additions).
  • Incorporar: bootstrapRunTx, appendAndEnqueueTx, la semántica del outbox, RunMetadata, y eliminar projectSnapshot (la proyección no debe ser responsabilidad del store).
  • Actualizar el changelog del contrato con la razón del cambio.

docs.title: W1-3 — Definir ownership de RunCancelled (nuevo ADR o enmienda a ADR-0011)
docs.text:
Problema: ADR-0011 define que el adapter emite RunStarted. No existe decisión equivalente para RunCancelled. WorkflowEngine.cancelRun emite RunCancelled directamente después de que adapter.cancelRun() retorna. Para Temporal y Conductor, cancelRun envía una señal de cancelación — el workflow no se ha cancelado aún cuando la llamada retorna.

Tarea:

  • Decidir y documentar: ¿quién emite RunCancelled?
  • Opción A: El adapter emite RunCancelled desde dentro del contexto de ejecución del workflow (cuando el workflow procesa la cancelación). El engine no emite RunCancelled.
  • Opción B: El engine emite RunCancelled como evento de intención ("se solicitó cancelación"). El adapter emite un evento separado cuando la cancelación efectiva ocurre (nuevo event type RunTerminated).
  • Escribir ADR-0017 con la decisión.
  • Actualizar WorkflowEngine.cancelRun para reflejar la decisión.

Criterio de aceptación:

  • ADR-0017 aprobado y referenciado desde ADR-0011.
  • WorkflowEngine.cancelRun implementa la decisión sin ambigüedad.
  • Projector maneja la transición de estado de forma consistente con la decisión.

docs.title: W1-4 — Definir fórmula normativa para señales en contrato (SignalsAndAuth v1.1)
docs.text:
Problema: RunEvents.v2.0.md §1.1 excluye señales del scope y los refiere a "SignalsAndAuth v1.1 (pending publication)". Ese documento no existe. La implementación usa una fórmula ad-hoc no contractual.

Tarea:

  • Publicar SignalsAndAuth.v1.1.md en docs/architecture/engine/contracts/engine/.
  • Incluir: event types de señales (SignalAccepted, SignalRejected), idempotency key formula, envelope fields requeridos.
  • Actualizar referencias en RunEvents.v2.0.md y IWorkflowEngine.v2.0.md.

docs.title: W1-5 — Avanzar ADRs Proposed/Pending a Accepted tras verificar implementación
docs.text:
Según ADR_Status_Board_Extensive.md, varios ADRs están en estado Proposed/Pending con código parcialmente implementado.

ADR Estado actual Acción ADR-0013 (bootstrapRunTx) Proposed bootstrapRunTx existe en código. Verificar criterios del status board → marcar Accepted. ADR-0011 (RunStarted ownership) Approved Verificar que implementación de Temporal emite RunStarted desde workflow. Si sí → marcar Accepted. ADR-0012 (plan integrity) Pending No implementado. Permanece Pending hasta W0-1/W0-2/W0-3 completados. ADR-0014 (run-driven model) Proposed Implementado parcialmente (IProviderAdapter acepta plan, no planRef). Se cierra junto con W0-2. ADR-0015 (getRunStatus) Proposed Se cierra junto con W0-6. ADR-0016 (logicalAttemptId) Proposed Se cierra junto con W3-2.

Criterio: Un ADR no puede marcarse Accepted sin: código conforme + test que prueba el invariante + CI verde.

docs.title: WAVE 2 — Critical Path Abierto (Issues existentes)
docs.text: Issues del ROADMAP.md existente. Los listamos con sus dependencias reales tras el análisis.

docs.title: W2-1 — PostgresStateStore MVP (#6)
docs.text:
Bloqueado por: W0-4 (la interfaz de IRunStateStore cambia al eliminar saveProviderRef), W1-2 (contrato actualizado).

Requisitos adicionales del análisis:

  • DDL debe incluir particionamiento por tenant_id + rango de tiempo en run_events. Sin particionamiento, los queries de listEvents se degradan a O(total events) a escala.
  • Índice único en (run_id, idempotency_key) — obligatorio por contrato.
  • Índice único en (run_id, run_seq) — obligatorio por contrato.
  • bootstrapRunTx debe ser una única transacción BEGIN; INSERT run_metadata; INSERT run_events; INSERT outbox; COMMIT;.
  • appendAndEnqueueTx debe incluir upsert de snapshot (W0-7).
  • run_seq debe generarse con SELECT nextval('run_seq_seq_for_' || run_id) o equivalent para evitar contention — no MAX(run_seq) + 1.

Criterio de aceptación (adicional al existente en #6):

  • EXPLAIN ANALYZE en listEvents(runId) para 10K eventos muestra Index Scan, no Seq Scan.
  • bootstrapRunTx con run_id duplicado retorna RUN_ALREADY_EXISTS, no error de Postgres sin manejar.
  • Partición por tiempo definida en la migración inicial.

docs.title: W2-2 — TemporalAdapter full implementation (#68)
docs.text:
Bloqueado por: W0-2 (firma startRun(planRef)), W0-3 (@dvt/plan-verifier), W0-4 (no más saveProviderRef).

Requisitos adicionales del análisis:

  • RunStarted DEBE emitirse como primera operación dentro del workflow function body, antes de scheduling de activities (ADR-0011).
  • logicalAttemptId DEBE almacenarse en el workflow state (no derivarse de DB). Esto requiere que el workflow tenga una variable logicalAttemptId que se pasa como input a cada activity.
  • UUID v4 dentro del workflow code DEBE usar workflow.uuid4() de Temporal TypeScript SDK, no randomUUID de Node.js (no determinista en workflow context).
  • signal(RETRY_STEP/RETRY_RUN) puede quedar como SignalNotImplementedError en Phase 1 pero debe estar documentado explícitamente en el adapter.
  • El adapter DEBE usar @dvt/plan-verifier para fetch + SHA-256 + schema + identity.

docs.title: W2-3 — Temporal Interpreter Workflow (#15)
docs.text:
Requisitos adicionales del análisis:

  • La resolución de dependsOn en el plan (qué steps ejecutar en paralelo, cuáles deben esperar) es responsabilidad del Interpreter. El plan define el DAG; el Interpreter lo camina.
  • Step execution en paralelo: usar workflow.executeActivity con Promise.all para steps sin dependencias entre sí.
  • Error en un step: emitir StepFailed → según RetryBackoffPolicy en el plan, decidir si reintentar (incrementar logicalAttemptId) o terminar con RunFailed.
  • La política de retry del plan (RetryBackoffPolicy) no existe aún — para Phase 1, usar retry policy fija (hardcoded 3 intentos, backoff exponencial).

docs.title: W2-4 — Snapshot write-through en PostgresStateStore (#6 sub-task)
docs.text:
Ver W0-7. Debe hacerse como parte de la implementación del PostgresStateStore, no como add-on posterior. appendAndEnqueueTx en Postgres debe:

  1. INSERT evento en run_events
  2. INSERT en outbox
  3. UPSERT snapshot en run_snapshots
  4. COMMIT

Los cuatro en una sola transacción.

docs.title: WAVE 3 — Fundamentos Operacionales
docs.text: Sin estas tareas, la Phase 1.5 (hardening) no puede validarse correctamente.

docs.title: W3-1 — Stuck-run detection: SLA de RunQueued → RunStarted
docs.text:
Problema: Un run puede quedarse en RunQueued indefinidamente si el Temporal worker está caído. No hay timeout ni alerta definida.

Tarea:

  • Definir SLA máximo para RunQueued → RunStarted (sugerencia: 5 minutos configurable por tenant).
  • Implementar un proceso background (job/cron) que detecte runs en RunQueued más de N minutos y emita RunFailed con payload.reason = 'QUEUED_TIMEOUT'.
  • Agregar alert en Grafana/Prometheus: runs_stuck_in_queued_gt_threshold.
  • Documentar el SLA en un nuevo documento SLADefinitions.v1.md.

Criterio de aceptación:

  • Test de integración: run en RunQueued > threshold → RunFailed emitido automáticamente.
  • Métrica dvt.run.queued_timeout_total existe y es incrementada.

docs.title: W3-2 — Implementar logicalAttemptId tracking en Temporal workflow state (ADR-0016 completo)
docs.text:
Problema actual: buildRunEvent hardcodea logicalAttemptId: 1 en todos los eventos emitidos por el engine. Para los eventos emitidos por el Temporal adapter (StepStarted, StepFailed, etc.) el logicalAttemptId debe rastrearse en el workflow state.

Tarea:

  • En el Temporal Interpreter Workflow: mantener variable logicalAttemptId: number en el workflow state, inicializado en 1.
  • Pasar logicalAttemptId como parámetro de entrada a cada activity que emita eventos.
  • Cuando se reciba un signal RETRY_STEP o RETRY_RUN: incrementar logicalAttemptId en el workflow state antes de re-ejecutar.
  • El engine nunca lee logicalAttemptId de la DB para emitirlo — siempre viene del workflow state.

Criterio de aceptación:

  • Un run con 2 retries de un step tiene eventos con logicalAttemptId 1, 2, 3 respectivamente.
  • El idempotencyKey del step en intento 2 es diferente al del intento 1 (derivación es por logicalAttemptId).
  • El Temporal workflow replay reproduce el mismo logicalAttemptId sin tocar la DB.
  • ADR-0016 marcado Accepted tras verificación.

docs.title: W3-3 — Paginación en listEvents y listRuns
docs.text:
Problema: IRunStateStore.listEvents(runId) retorna todos los eventos sin límite. Para un run de 1000 nodos dbt, son 2000+ rows en una sola query.

Tarea:

  • Agregar parámetros { afterSeq?: number; limit?: number } a listEvents en IRunStateStore.
  • Agregar { cursor?: string; limit?: number } a listRuns (cursor-based pagination).
  • Actualizar IRunStateStore.v2.1.md con las firmas.
  • WorkflowEngine.getRunStatus debe usar paginación cuando hace full replay.
  • Definir límite máximo por default: limit = 500 para listEvents, limit = 50 para listRuns.

docs.title: W3-4 — Política de retención de eventos
docs.text:
Problema: El event log es append-only sin archival. Crecerá sin límite.

Tarea:

  • Definir y documentar en RetentionPolicy.v1.md:
  • Hot tier (Postgres): 90 días para runs completados/fallidos; runs activos sin expiración.
  • Cold tier (S3/GCS): 7 años (requerimiento SOC2 referenciado en AuditLog.v1.md).
  • Archival trigger: runs terminados (COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED) con persistedAt > 90 días.
  • Implementar job de archival que serializa eventos a NDJSON, los sube a object storage, y borra de Postgres.
  • Agregar archived_at a run_metadata para saber si un run fue archivado.
  • listEvents debe indicar si los eventos fueron archivados y el URI del archivo.

docs.title: W3-5 — Estrategia de migración de eventos v1 → v2
docs.text:
Problema: Los contratos cambiaron de v1 a v2 (se agregó planId/planVersion al idempotencyKey, se removió occurredAt, se separaron emittedAt/persistedAt). No hay una guía de qué hacer con eventos v1 en el log.

Tarea:

  • Documentar en ContractMigrationGuide.v1-v2.md:
  • Qué campos cambiaron y cómo normalizarlos.
  • Ventana de compatibilidad (sugerencia: 30 días post-cutover, projectors aceptan ambos formatos).
  • Qué hacer con eventos v1 que no tienen planId/planVersion — definir valor de relleno ("legacy" / "0").
  • Procedimiento de rollback si se detectan eventos v1 en producción tras cutover.
  • Implementar normalización en el projector para campos faltantes con fallback documentado.

docs.title: W3-6 — Aislamiento de tenants a nivel de base de datos
docs.text:
Problema actual: El aislamiento de tenants es solo via IAuthorizer.assertTenantAccess(). Si una query no filtra por tenantId, los datos de diferentes tenants pueden mezclarse.

Tarea:

  • Todas las queries en PostgresStateStore deben incluir WHERE tenant_id = $1 como primer filtro, sin excepción.
  • Agregar índices que incluyan tenant_id como primera columna para queries frecuentes.
  • Implementar test de aislamiento: tenant A no puede ver eventos de tenant B aunque conozca el runId.
  • Opcionalmente: Row Level Security (RLS) en Postgres como capa de defensa adicional.

docs.title: W3-7 — Definir y documentar el modelo de concurrencia para startRun
docs.text:
Problema: ensureRunDoesNotExist + bootstrapRunTx tienen una ventana de race condition entre el check y la inserción. La guarda de RUN_ALREADY_EXISTS de la DB es la última línea de defensa.

Tarea:

  • Documentar el comportamiento esperado en dos escenarios:
  • Mismo runId enviado dos veces concurrentemente: el segundo debe recibir RUN_ALREADY_EXISTS (409).
  • Mismo runId con mismo plan (idempotent retry): ¿retornar el EngineRunRef existente o rechazar?
  • Implementar el comportamiento documentado.
  • Eliminar el check de ensureRunDoesNotExist separado — es redundante si bootstrapRunTx ya maneja el conflicto con RUN_ALREADY_EXISTS. O dejarlo como fast-fail antes de la operación costosa del adapter.

docs.title: WAVE 4 — Hardening (Phase 1.5 del ROADMAP existente)
docs.text: Prerrequisito: WAVE 0 completado. Sin correctness, el load testing valida comportamiento incorrecto.

docs.title: W4-1 — Load Testing con k6 (issue #18)
docs.text:
Requisito adicional del análisis: El test de carga debe incluir:

  • Stress test de runSeq contention: 100 steps en paralelo para el mismo run → verificar que runSeq es monotónico sin gaps incorrectos.
  • Test de listEvents(runId) para runs de 1000 steps: latencia p99 < 50ms con snapshot habilitado vs sin snapshot.
  • Test de bootstrapRunTx bajo concurrencia: 1000 runs simultáneos de diferentes tenants → zero RUN_ALREADY_EXISTS falsos positivos.

docs.title: W4-2 — Chaos Engineering
docs.text:
Adicional a lo planificado:

  • Crash del process Node.js entre adapter.startRun() y bootstrapRunTx — verificar compensación (W0-4).
  • Crash del OutboxWorker con outbox con 1000 pendientes — verificar at-least-once delivery sin duplicados en el estado derivado.
  • Restart de un Temporal worker con un workflow activo — verificar que logicalAttemptId sobrevive el replay (W3-2).

docs.title: W4-3 — Backpressure en OutboxWorker
docs.text:
Problema identificado: No hay backpressure definido en el procesamiento del outbox. Si el event bus es lento, el outbox crece sin límite.

Tarea:

  • Implementar BACKPRESSURE_ON signal cuando el queue depth del outbox supera umbral configurable (ej: 10K pending).
  • BACKPRESSURE_OFF cuando baja de umbral de recovery.
  • Métrica dvt.outbox.pending_count visible en Prometheus.
  • Documentar en el roadmap existente como sub-tarea de #18.

docs.title: WAVE 5 — Expansión de Plataforma (Phase 2+)
docs.text: No iniciar hasta que WAVE 0 + WAVE 1 + critical path WAVE 2 estén completados.

docs.title: W5-1 — Implementar IExecutionPlanner port + implementación mínima
docs.text:
Estado actual: No existe. Es el tercer pilar del mantra "planner / engine / state".

Tarea:

  • Crear packages/@dvt/planner/:
  • IExecutionPlanner port: plan(spec: RunSpec): Promise<ExecutionPlan>
  • RunSpec type: qué correr, con qué selección, en qué entorno
  • BasicPlanner implementación: construye un ExecutionPlan desde un dbt manifest
  • DAGAnalyzer: parsea manifest.json, construye grafo de dependencias, ordena steps por topología.
  • No incluir CostImpactEstimator en Phase 1 del planner — es un enhancement, no un bloqueador.

Criterio de aceptación:

  • BasicPlanner.plan({ manifest, selection }) retorna ExecutionPlan válido con steps en orden topológico.
  • Tests: plan de 5 nodos con dependencias → steps en orden correcto → engine puede ejecutarlos.

docs.title: W5-2 — Conductor Adapter (post-Temporal hardening)
docs.text:
Prerrequisito: Temporal adapter en producción verificado. Los semantic gaps identificados deben estar documentados antes de comenzar:

  1. cancelRun timing: En Conductor, terminate es asíncrono. La decisión de ADR-0017 (W1-3) debe estar implementada antes de escribir una línea de ConductorAdapter.
  2. logicalAttemptId: Conductor no expone attempt counts nativos a nivel de run. La estrategia de tracking debe definirse antes de implementar.
  3. RunStarted ownership: Conductor define en qué punto "el workflow empieza ejecutando". Esto debe mapearse al mismo criterio de ADR-0011.

docs.title: W5-3 — Plugin System: fundación
docs.text:
Prerrequisito: IExecutionPlanner existe (W5-1), IProviderAdapter estabilizado (W0-2).

Tarea: Solo la fundación, no un sistema completo:

  • PluginManifest schema (capabilities, permissions, UI modules) — definir como JSON Schema + zod.
  • PluginRegistry: carga manifests, valida capabilities, no ejecuta nada.
  • IPluginRuntime port: load(manifest), invoke(pluginId, method, ctx), unload(pluginId).
  • NO comenzar con la sandbox de ejecución hasta que IPluginRuntime sea estable.
  • Eliminar vm2 como opción de sandbox — tiene historial de vulnerabilidades documentadas. Usar worker_threads como default.

docs.title: Resumen de Dependencias Críticas
docs.text:
W0-1 ──┐
W0-2 ──┼──► W0-3 (@dvt/plan-verifier) ──► W2-2 (TemporalAdapter)
W0-4 ──┘
         │
         └──► W2-1 (PostgresStateStore) ──► W4-1 (Load Testing)

W1-1 ──► (unblocks new adapter implementors)
W1-2 ──► W2-1
W1-3 ──► W2-2, W5-2

W0-6 ──► W3-1 (stuck-run detection sin provider coupling)
W0-7 ──► W3-3 (pagination + snapshot)

W2-1 + W2-2 + W2-3 ──► W4-1 (load testing)
W4-1 + W4-2 ──► W5-1 (planner)
W5-1 ──► W5-2 (Conductor), W5-3 (plugins)

docs.title: Tareas que NO deben empezarse antes de tiempo
docs.text: Tarea Razón para esperar Snowflake Cost Attribution Sin runs en producción, cualquier modelo es especulativo. QUERY_HISTORY no es síncrono. Delay a post-Phase 2. UI: Graph Canvas / Diff View / Lineage View Depende de ArtifactsParser y LineageStore que no existen. Build el backend primero. Conductor Adapter completo Los semantic gaps (cancelRun, logicalAttemptId) requieren que ADR-0017 exista y que Temporal esté en producción verificado. requiresCapabilities validation real Actualmente tira error si capabilities.length > 0. No construir el sistema de capabilities hasta que IExecutionPlanner exista.

docs.title: Métricas de progreso sugeridas
docs.text:
Para cada WAVE, la definición de "Done" es:

WAVE Done cuando... WAVE 0 Todos los tests de WorkflowEngine pasan sin mockear IPlanFetcher; saveProviderRef eliminado; getRunStatus no llama al adapter; golden vectors de señales en contrato. WAVE 1 ADR-0010 anotado; IRunStateStore.v2.1.md publicado; ADR-0017 aprobado; SignalsAndAuth.v1.1.md publicado. WAVE 2 Golden paths de Phase 1 MVP pasan con PostgresStateStore real + TemporalAdapter real. WAVE 3 Stuck-run test pasa; retención definida; listEvents paginado; contract migration guide existe. WAVE 4 Load test 500 events/sec sostenido 4h; chaos suite pasa; idempotency torture 1M events sin corrupción. WAVE 5 BasicPlanner retorna plan válido desde manifest dbt real; plugin manifest cargado y validado.

Generado desde revisión arquitectónica de 2026-02-21. Complementa ROADMAP.md — no lo reemplaza.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This document defines the automation required to enforce ADR-0000.

Without automation, traceability becomes ceremonial.

docs.title: 1. Header Validator
docs.text:
Script: node tools/traceability/validate-headers.js

Checks: - Presence of @baseline - ADR existence - ADR status == Accepted

docs.title: 2. Manifest Generator
docs.text:
node tools/traceability/generate-manifest.js

Outputs: - dist/traceability-manifest.json

docs.title: 3. Reverse ADR Coverage Check
docs.text:
node tools/traceability/validate-adr-coverage.js

Fails if: - Any Accepted ADR has no implementing file

docs.title: 4. Neo4j Publisher
docs.text:
Uses: https://github.com/neo4j/neo4j-javascript-driver

Publishes: (:File)-[:BASELINED_ON]->(:ADR)

docs.title: CI Example
docs.text:
name: ADR Governance
on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  governance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - run: node tools/traceability/validate-headers.js
      - run: node tools/traceability/generate-manifest.js
      - run: node tools/traceability/validate-adr-coverage.js

docs.text:

docs.text:
• ADR

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
graph TD
    File[File] -->|BASELINED_ON| ADR[ADR]
    Module[Module] -->|CONTAINS| File

- (:File)-\[:BASELINED_ON\]-\>(:ADR)
- (:Module)-\[:CONTAINS\]-\>(:File)

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
CREATE CONSTRAINT adr_number IF NOT EXISTS
FOR (a:ADR) REQUIRE a.number IS UNIQUE;

CREATE CONSTRAINT file_path IF NOT EXISTS
FOR (f:File) REQUIRE f.path IS UNIQUE;

CREATE CONSTRAINT module_name IF NOT EXISTS
FOR (m:Module) REQUIRE m.name IS UNIQUE;

docs.title: Example Query: ADRs without baselined files
docs.text:
MATCH (a:ADR {status:"Accepted"})
WHERE NOT (:File)-[:BASELINED_ON]->(a)
RETURN a.number, a.title;

docs.title: Example Query: Blast radius (files affected by ADR)
docs.text:
MATCH (a:ADR {number:$adr})<-[:BASELINED_ON]-(f:File)
RETURN f.path;

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Architecture diagrams, explanations, and adapter specifications for the DVT engine.

See architecture/engine/INDEX.md for engine-specific documentation.

docs.title: DVT Architecture Analysis
docs.text: Date: 2026-02-13 Status: Updated after monorepo cleanup

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text:
The repository is now aligned around a package-oriented monorepo layout with canonical code under packages/*.

Key improvements already delivered:

  • CI and scripts now target package-scoped paths.
  • Contract/golden-path validation is wired to package tests.
  • Root documentation has been reduced and moved into structured docs/ sections.

docs.title: Current High-Level Structure
docs.text:
dvt/
├── packages/
│   ├── contracts/
│   ├── engine/
│   ├── adapter-postgres/
│   ├── adapter-temporal/
│   └── cli/
├── docs/
├── .github/
├── scripts/
├── CHANGELOG.md
├── ROADMAP.md
├── CONTRIBUTING.md
└── README.md

docs.title: What Improved
docs.text:
1. Path consistency

  2. Workflows and scripts no longer depend on legacy top-level test paths.

  3. Determinism validation flow

  4. Golden-path execution and hash comparison are integrated in CI.

  5. Documentation structure

  6. Non-core root docs were moved to focused sections under docs/.

  7. Windows compatibility

  8. Package test scripts now use options that avoid shell-specific failures.

docs.title: Remaining Gaps
docs.text:
1. Lint debt in legacy/adapter areas

  2. Existing parser/project-boundary and import-order issues remain.

  3. Adapter completion

  4. Full Temporal/Conductor implementation and parity checks are still in progress.

  5. Documentation normalization

  6. Remaining markdown files need final consistency and language review.

docs.title: Recommended Next Steps
docs.text:
1. Stabilize lint and type boundaries package-by-package.
  2. Complete adapter parity with deterministic contract tests.
  3. Expand golden-path fixtures and maintain hash baseline discipline.
  4. Finalize documentation normalization and cross-link integrity checks.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text: The current architecture is adequate for the project context (contracts-first workflow engine with adapter boundaries in a monorepo), with operational deviations that should be addressed in the short term.

docs.title: What is working well
docs.text:
1. Package boundaries are clear

  2. Monorepo package split (contracts, engine, adapters, cli) remains coherent with domain responsibilities.

  3. Core dependency injection and testability

  4. The engine core uses explicit dependency contracts via WorkflowEngineDeps, improving isolation and unit/integration testing.

  5. Security and contract guards happen early

  6. Run start flow enforces plan policy, tenant authorization, and integrity validation before provider execution.

  7. Deterministic event persistence model

  8. Idempotency and event append flow remain aligned with deterministic execution constraints.

docs.title: Detected deviations and risks
docs.text:
1. Temporal integration test fragility

  2. Integration lifecycle (worker.run/shutdown/environment teardown) still shows risk of flaky behavior under time-skipping/native connection scenarios.

  3. Release governance drift

  4. Documentation and tooling references are not fully converged on a single release automation path yet.

  5. Architecture hardening debt remains open

  6. Lint boundary debt and adapter parity are still active, reducing confidence in long-term maintainability if left unresolved.

docs.title: Priority actions (recommended order)
docs.text:
1. Stabilize Temporal integration lifecycle policy

  2. Standardize teardown order and assert no leaked worker references in integration tests.

  3. Converge release process documentation and automation

  4. Keep one canonical release flow and remove parallel/legacy ambiguity.

  5. Enforce architectural boundaries with tooling

  6. Adopt/enable boundary validation and targeted static rules to prevent layer erosion.

  7. Turn gaps into measurable exit criteria

  8. Define explicit targets (flake rate, coverage by package, pass stability window) and align them with roadmap checkpoints.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
• pnpm -r build succeeds.
  • pnpm -r test succeeds for packages with tests.
  • CI workflows reference only canonical package paths.
  • Documentation index and strategic docs reflect current implementation state.

Last updated: 2026-02-13

docs.title: Ddd cqrs
docs.text:
# DDD + CQRS guidelines (summary)

This document describes the minimal conventions for structuring packages using Domain-Driven Design and a lightweight CQRS approach.

Folder conventions (in `@dvt/engine`):

- `src/domain/` — Entities, Value Objects, Aggregates, Domain Services, Repository interfaces.
- `src/application/` — Use cases, Commands, Command Handlers, DTOs, Application Services.
- `src/infrastructure/` — Implementations of repository/adapters (Postgres, Temporal), external integrations.
- `src/transport/` — API adapters, event publishers, workers.
- `src/cqrs/` — Command bus, Query bus, Event handlers (in-process minimal implementations).

Traceability conventions:

- All generated artifacts must include `@baseline ADR-0000` in file headers.
- Use ADR references in commits and manifest files.

Example: Command handler header

```typescript
/**
 * @file StartRunHandler.ts
 * @baseline ADR-0000
 * @decision ADR-0004, ADR-0005
 */
```

Testing:

  • Keep unit tests close to implementation (same package under test/ or src/__tests__).
  • Add conformance/golden vector tests for contracts in @dvt/contracts.

CI:

  • Ensure pnpm -r build and pnpm -r test run the added packages.

docs.title: Review 20260222
docs.text:
DVT+ Architectural Review Role: Principal Software Architect

Date: 2026-02-22

Sources: ADRs 0003–0016, IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP_FROM_REVIEW.md, WorkflowEngine.ts, @dvt/ packages, v2 architecture diagram, planning docs

  1. Conceptual Soundness The core thesis — domain-owned execution semantics over adapter-agnostic infrastructure — is architecturally correct. The insight that "Temporal's internal state is not the source of truth; the event log is" is the most important decision in the system. Any design that derives business state from a workflow engine's internal APIs ends up coupled to that engine permanently. DVT+ avoids this.

The three-tier mantra (planner / engine / state) maps cleanly to three responsibilities:

Planner: what to execute and in what order Engine: when to execute and what the lifecycle transitions are State: that it happened, immutably The problem is that only one tier is real. The planner doesn't exist as implemented code. The state store is a stub. The engine is implemented and architecturally sound, but it's a bridge to infrastructure that isn't there yet.

The ADR process is a genuine strength. Twenty-six ADRs with explicit acceptance criteria, status boards, and traceability is not normal for a pre-production system. Most teams write ADRs post-incident. This one wrote them upfront and used them as implementation guides — the IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP_FROM_REVIEW.md demonstrates this directly, finding 7 active bugs by comparing ADR text to code. That's architecture as a tool, not decoration.

There is a concept drift problem. Some documents describe DVT+ as a "dbt orchestration platform." Others describe a "generic deterministic workflow engine." The v2 architecture diagram shows React Flow canvas, diff views, lineage views, Snowflake cost attribution, a plugin system with sandbox execution, GraphQL API, and git sync — that's not a workflow engine, it's a platform product with 3+ years of scope. The conceptual model shifts depending on which document you're reading. This is not an engine architecture flaw. It is a product scope problem that will generate architectural pressure and mis-prioritization over time.

  1. Architectural Risk Map Risk Severity Certainty Status PostgresStateStore not implemented Critical Certain Open — MVP cannot persist state

No IExecutionPlanner interface High Certain Open — users produce ExecutionPlans with no contract No pagination in listEvents High Certain Open — full scan for 1000-step dbt runs No stuck-run detection High Certain Open — runs can be stranded in QUEUED indefinitely Tenant isolation is WHERE-clause only High High Open — no RLS, one query bug crosses tenants uuid generation in Temporal workflow context High High Open — must use workflow.uuid4(), not randomUUID() ADR-to-code drift High Certain Ongoing — 6 ADRs in Proposed/Pending with partial implementation Two-phase write gap (bootstrapRunTx) Critical Fixed Resolved this session vm2 referenced for plugin sandbox Critical Low-but-real Flagged in roadmap — vm2 has documented escape vulnerabilities No event retention/archival policy Medium Certain Open — event log grows without bound runSeq contention under parallel steps Medium High Open — if implemented as MAX+1, concurrent appends contend

Calls adapter first, then bootstrapRunTx with runRef included Emits RunCancelRequested (intent) not RunCancelled (terminal) Uses SHA-256 idempotency keys that exclude tenantId and payload What remains wrong:

  1. getRunStatus is not a pure read model. getRunStatus calls adapter.getRunStatus() with a 30-second timeout. ADR-0015 is unambiguous: "The default read path MUST NOT call the provider." In multi-replica deployments, the in-process circuitStateByProvider map is useless — each replica holds independent circuit state. A Temporal worker restart causes 30-second latency spikes in every status query across every replica.

  2. The circuit breaker pattern is wrong by design. circuitStateByProvider: Map inside WorkflowEngine is process-local. It provides false safety in any deployment beyond a single Node.js instance. Circuit breakers must be shared state — Redis, or an external circuit breaker service. This component needs to be removed from the engine and replaced with infrastructure-level protection.

  3. capabilities validation is disabled. requiresCapabilities throws if capabilities.length > 0. Any plan that declares capabilities (which is the correct thing to do) will fail at runtime before an adapter is reached. This means the capabilities field in the plan schema is currently a runtime landmine.

    4. This is a significant gap for three reasons:

    Third, retry policy in the plan schema is defined but enforced by nothing. RetryBackoffPolicy exists as a field. No component reads it and applies it during step failure handling. The roadmap correctly specifies hardcoded 3-retry policy for Phase 1, but that decision should be in a document, not implicit in code. 5. State & Metadata Layer Review

    Append-only run_events as source of truth Monotonic run_seq per runId Snapshot as optimistic cache for O(1) reads Outbox pattern for reliable at-least-once delivery to the event bus bootstrapRunTx as single atomic start point (now includes provider refs)

    1. No PostgresStateStore. The only persistence is whatever in-memory implementation exists for tests. DVT+ cannot be deployed. There is no Phase 1 MVP without this.

    2. Snapshot write-through is not implemented (W0-7). After each appendAndEnqueueTx, the snapshot is not updated. Every getRunStatus call requires full event replay via listEvents. For a dbt run with 1000 nodes, this is 2000+ rows fetched per status query. Under production load, listEvents will be the top-1 query by cost in the database.

    3. Plugin System Evaluation The plugin system does not exist. What exists: a box in the v2 architecture diagram, a note in the roadmap that vm2 should not be used, and references to IPluginRuntime as a planned interface.

    The recommendation to eliminate vm2 is correct. vm2 has documented sandbox escape vulnerabilities. It is not safe for production execution of user-provided code regardless of how carefully it is configured. The alternatives — worker_threads with strict IPC, V8 isolates (Deno-style), or container-per-plugin — are all more complex than vm2 for a reason. Secure plugin execution is genuinely hard.

    The plugin system as described in the v2 architecture (manifest, sandbox runtime, API surface, custom plugin types) is 6–12 months of engineering work post-engine-stability. The correct decision is in the roadmap: do not start the plugin system until IExecutionPlanner and IProviderAdapter are stable and in production. Building the extension surface before the product is validated is how systems end up with elaborate plugin infrastructure and no working core.

    The specific concern: if plugins can invoke adapter methods or access run state, the plugin API surface must be designed alongside those interfaces. A plugin API designed before IProviderAdapter is stable will either be too narrow (forcing breaking changes later) or too broad (creating a security boundary that's impossible to enforce). 7. What Is Overbuilt?

    1. Architecture diagram scope. The v2 diagram includes React Flow canvas, Snowflake cost attribution, plugin sandbox, diff view, lineage view, GraphQL API, and git sync. This is a 3-5 year product roadmap drawn as if it were current architecture. Aspirational diagrams in early-stage systems mislead planning by creating a false picture of completeness.

    2. ADR volume for unbuilt components. ADR-0002 (Neo4j as knowledge graph repository) and ADR-0006 (contract tooling governance) describe infrastructure with no code in the repository. Writing ADRs for hypothetical components produces documentation debt, not decision clarity. ADRs should follow implemented decisions, not precede unimplemented ones.

    3. @dvt/traceability-service package. This directory exists. The traceability infrastructure it represents (Neo4j, graph model, query surface) is completely unbuilt. Premature package definition without implementation creates dead code that accumulates maintenance surface.

    4. What Is Underbuilt?

    5. TemporalAdapter (real, not stub). Second critical path item. Nothing executes without it.

    6. Stuck-run detection. No mechanism exists to detect or recover from runs stranded in QUEUED. In production, a Temporal worker restart will orphan queued runs silently.

    7. Multi-tenancy enforcement depth. Tenant isolation is one missing WHERE clause away from a data breach. No Row Level Security in Postgres. No audit log of access patterns. No per-tenant connection isolation.

    8. Recovery procedures. What happens when Postgres is unavailable mid-transaction? When Temporal's cluster is unreachable for 30 minutes? When bootstrapRunTx partially commits? No documented recovery procedure exists. This is not optional for a system that positions itself as "reliable execution for critical workflows."

    9. Scalability Outlook (3-Year Horizon)

    Append-only event log partitioned by tenant_id + time scales to millions of runs with correct indexing. Snapshot write-through (W0-7 when implemented) decouples read latency from event log size. Adapter-first pattern means adding Conductor or BullMQ is additive, not disruptive to the engine.

    In-process circuit breaker. Doesn't scale past one replica. Has to be removed.

    listEvents without pagination. Unbounded. For a run with 1000 steps and 2000 events, this is megabytes per status query at production call rates. Projection recomputation without snapshots. Without snapshot write-through, every getRunStatus call triggers a full event replay. At 10 status queries per second per run across 100 concurrent runs = 1000 listEvents queries/second. With 2000 events per run, that's 2 million rows/second just for status queries.

    If plugins enter production under the worker_threads model, the horizontal scaling limit is roughly 500 concurrent plugin invocations per Node.js process before thread pool saturation.

    1. Architectural Scorecard Dimension Score Assessment Operational Readiness 2/10 No stuck-run detection, no pagination, no retention policy, no recovery playbook, no dashboards. Security Posture 4/10 IAuthorizer exists. Tenant isolation is WHERE-clause only. No RLS. vm2 risk documented not eliminated. Scalability Design 6/10 Correct patterns (event sourcing, adapters, outbox). runSeq contention and circuit breaker are concrete gaps.

    2. Implement W0-6 (getRunStatus read-path separation) as part of PostgresStateStore work. The read path must serve from the event log only. Separate enrichRunStatus if provider enrichment is needed for specific use cases. Remove circuitStateByProvider from the engine. Put circuit breaking in infrastructure.

    3. Eliminate vm2 from all planning documents and code comments now, not when the plugin system starts. The moment vm2 appears in a code file, it will be used. Specify the secure alternative — worker_threads with strict IPC message validation, or container-per-plugin — before any plugin execution code is written.

    61 lines

docs.title: User Preferences
docs.text:
• Spanish/English mixed (responds in same language used)
  • Concise surgical edits preferred
  • ADR traceability on all changes The architectural review is complete. Key findings in summary:

Score: 5.4/10 — The engine abstraction is conceptually sound and the ADR discipline is real, but the implementation gap is large: no persistent state store, no real adapter, no planner, and several active correctness bugs. Top 3 blockers: PostgresStateStore, TemporalAdapter, and the logicalAttemptId hardcoded-to-1 bug (which silently corrupts retry state via idempotency key collisions). Biggest overbuilding risk: The v2 architecture diagram includes 3–5 years of product scope, which distorts planning and hides the gap between current state and running software. Most underestimated gap: @dvt/plan-verifier doesn't exist — without it, every adapter will implement SHA-256 verification independently and they will drift. The IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP_FROM_REVIEW.md already has the correct wave structure. The review validates it and adds the scoring context for prioritization decisions.

  1. Build PostgresStateStore before anything else. The engine is architecturally correct. It has nowhere to persist state. All correctness investments — the ADR framework, the golden path tests, the bootstrapRunTx work — are unverifiable without a real store. Nothing else ships without this. Task:Explore PostgresStateStore existing code

Changes made:

adapter-postgres/src/types.ts

EventType: added 'RunCancelRequested' — the engine emits this; without it the adapter stored it as an unknown type and the snapshot projector silently ignored it WorkflowSnapshot: added cancelling: boolean — matches WorkflowSnapshot in engine's runEvents.ts; without it every snapshot read by the engine would fail structural type checks IRunStateStore interface: removed saveProviderRef — ADR-0013/0014 mandates adapter-first; the engine no longer calls this method adapter-postgres/src/PostgresStateStoreAdapter.ts

Added handleRunCancelRequested function: sets snap.cancelling = true Added case 'RunCancelRequested' to applyEventToSnapshot switch Fixed seed object in appendEventsTxWithClient: added cancelling: false — without this the initial snapshot written on bootstrap was structurally incomplete Added run_metadata_tenant_created_idx in ensureIndexes — listRuns(tenantId) was doing a full table scan

Removed saveProviderRef from the interface — the engine removed the call in this session; the interface needed to follow adapter-temporal/src/engine-types.ts

Removed saveProviderRef from the local IRunStateStore copy — kept in sync with the canonical interface adapter-postgres/test/smoke.test.ts

Replaced the three old tests (which used deprecated saveRunMetadata and appendEventsTx, and were missing planId/planVersion) with 9 focused tests covering: bootstrapRunTx atomicity, RUN_ALREADY_EXISTS, idempotency, snapshot write-through (W0-7), the full RunCancelRequested → cancelling=true → RunCancelled flow (ADR-0007), outbox delivery lifecycle, dead-letter promotion, and multi-tenant listRuns isolation 12/12 passing. What changed and why:

WorkflowEngine.ts

Removed Reason CircuitState interface Process-local circuit breaker is useless in multi-replica circuitStateByProvider field Same — each replica held independent state withCircuitBreaker method Deleted entirely circuitBreaker from WorkflowEngineDeps No caller in the engine needs it now getRunStatus is now 8 lines: resolve meta → assert tenant → read snapshot → return. No adapter call. No timeout. No circuit breaker. Latency is bounded by the state store only.

enrichRunStatus is the new method for cases where provider substatus is needed — reads the same snapshot base, then calls adapter.getRunStatus with withTimeout. It throws if the adapter fails (no silent swallow — the caller owns the retry/fallback decision, which is where circuit breaking belongs: at the HTTP handler, behind a dedicated endpoint, with a shared Redis-backed breaker).

IWorkflowEngine.v1_1_1.ts — enrichRunStatus added with ADR-0015 doc comments distinguishing the two methods.

WorkflowEngine.test.ts — the old test was asserting the swallow behavior that no longer exists. Replaced with three tests: one proving the adapter is never called on getRunStatus, one verifying enrichRunStatus merges substatus correctly, one verifying enrichRunStatus propagates adapter failures rather than hiding them. What was done ExecutionPlan interface (executionPlan.ts:1) — v1.0.0 → v1.1.0:

contractVersion: string — required; the adapter rejects plans with unknown versions plannerVersion?: string — optional; semver of the planner binary plannerGitSha?: string — optional; 40-char SHA for traceability generatedAt?: string — optional; ISO UTC timestamp of generation MockAdapter (MockAdapter.ts:37):

Interface shape: required fields present, optional fields are optional contractVersion validation: accepts "1.0.0", rejects "99.0.0" with PLAN_CONTRACT_VERSION_UNKNOWN Provenance fields: plan with all 4 new fields executes without error What was done capabilities.schema.json — added basic-execution to the normative enum (was missing despite being used in all plan fixtures)

adapters.capabilities.json — restructured from a JSON Schema document to a plain instance document; added mock adapter entry; temporal gets basic-execution + history.rotation; conductor gets basic-execution

ConductorAdapterStub — declares ['basic-execution', 'signal.pause.emulated', 'cancel.forced', 'workflow.fan.parallel', 'query.task.state', 'replay.task', 'signals.rate.limit']

capabilities.contract.test.ts — 13 tests:

6 engine gate tests (accept/reject/skip scenarios) 4 adapter declaration tests 3 matrix drift gate tests (CI guard: adapter.capabilities() must match

Resumen del fix Bug: logicalAttemptId hardcodeado a 1 en buildRunEvent y emitSignalDerivedRunEvent. En retry (Phase 2), los eventos del intento N producirían idempotency keys idénticas al intento 1 → deduplication silenciosa → corrupción de estado.

Fix:

Archivo Cambio runEvents.ts logicalAttemptId: number agregado a RunMetadata con doc comment WorkflowEngine.ts buildRunMetadata → logicalAttemptId: 1 (Phase 1). buildRunEvent y emitSignalDerivedRunEvent → leen meta.logicalAttemptId PostgresStateStoreAdapter.ts logicalAttemptId: 1 en ambos reconstruct (Phase 1, sin columna DB nueva) engine-types.ts Copia local de RunMetadata sincronizada authorizer.deny.test.ts Literal RunMetadata actualizado Phase 2: cuando el Planner soporte retry, setea logicalAttemptId > 1 en RunContext → engine lo pasa a buildRunMetadata → todos los eventos del nuevo intento tienen keys distintos → idempotency correcta automáticamente. Los dos comentarios // Phase 1: column not yet in schema en Postgres marcan el punto de extensión.

Hay que verificar dónde exactamente ocurre.

¿Por cuál quieres ir — uuid/determinismo en Temporal, paginación de listEvents, o stuck-run detection? Diagnóstico rápido: el workflow actual ya es correcto.

RunPlanWorkflow.ts: zero Node.js imports, zero randomUUID, zero Date.now() eventId() → ocurre en actividades (fuera del sandbox) → determinismo safe ✓ La nota del roadmap (W2-2) es un requisito prospectivo para cuando el TemporalAdapter real necesite generar UUIDs dentro del workflow. Lo que sí existe es el riesgo de que alguien introduzca randomUUID sin darse cuenta. Podemos sellarlo con una regla de ESLint en el tsconfig de workflows, o simplemente reconocer que es un guard futuro.

docs.title: Normative Contracts (v1.x)
docs.text:
• Immutable core: MUST sections never change without major version bump.
  • Backward compatible: v1.1 extends v1.0 without breaking.
  • Small & focused: 1-5 pages, tight prose, numbered sections.
  • Examples included: Code snippets, schemas, pseudocode.

How to version:

  • Bug fix or clarification → v1.1 (minor bump)
  • New optional capability → v1.2 (minor bump)
  • Breaking change → v2.0 (major bump, multi-month deprecation window)

docs.title: Adapter Specifications
docs.text:
• Status label: NORMATIVE (Phase 1+) or DRAFT (Phase 2+)
  • Scope: Adapter-specific implementation details + invariants
  • Limits documented: Timeouts, payload sizes, concurrency

How to extend:

  • New feature (e.g., custom task queue) → update spec, version bump
  • Limitation discovered → document, update parity matrix, consider emulation

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Phase 2 establishes two critical normative contracts that drive workflow execution:

  1. IProjectorAdapter: Event-to-state transformation (materialization)
  2. IWorkflowEngineAdapter: Workflow orchestration and execution

These contracts separate concerns between event sourcing (state store + outbox) and execution logic (engine + projection).

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
Specification Version: 1.0.0 Release Date: 2026-02-11 Status: Normative (MUST implement as specified)

This document follows the versioning policy defined in VERSIONING.md.

docs.title: Architecture Pattern
docs.text:
Event Stream → Projector → Materialized State
    ↓
Workflow Engine (uses State Store + Outbox)
    ↓
Step Execution (plugins/adapters)
    ↓
Events → Outbox → Delivery Worker

docs.title: Purpose - IProjectorAdapter
docs.text: Transform raw workflow events into queryable, materialized state.

docs.title: Key Methods - IProjectorAdapter
docs.text:
• projectEvent(): Apply single event to state
  • projectBatch(): Efficient batch processing
  • queryProjectedState(): Search materialized views
  • getWorkflowStateSnapshot(): Current state lookup
  • rebuildProjection(): Recovery from event log
  • clearProjection(): Cleanup/archival

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
• Idempotent: Same event → same state (safe to replay)
  • Ordered: Events MUST be applied in sequence to maintain causality
  • Durable: Projected state MUST survive failures
  • Searchable: Implementation MUST support queries by workflow/step/status

docs.title: Example Implementations - IProjectorAdapter
docs.text:
• Postgres: Denormalized tables (workflow_snapshots, step_summaries)
  • DynamoDB: GSI for workflow queries, event versioning
  • Elasticsearch: Real-time materialized views with aggregations
  • In-Memory: For tests (fast, no durability)

docs.title: Purpose - IWorkflowEngineAdapter
docs.text: Drive workflow execution through state transitions, step coordination, and failure recovery.

docs.title: Key Methods - IWorkflowEngineAdapter
docs.text:
• createRun(): Initialize workflow
  • startRun(): Begin execution
  • executeStep(): Execute single step
  • executeStepBatch(): Parallel step execution
  • pauseRun(): Graceful pause
  • resumeRun(): Resume from pause
  • terminateRun(): Final failure
  • getRunState(): State inspection
  • replayRun(): Determinism verification
  • archiveRun(): Completed workflow archival

docs.title: State Machine
docs.text:
INITIALIZING → RUNNING → PAUSED → RUNNING → COMPLETED
                  ↓
              FAILED (with retry logic)
                  ↓
            CANCELLED (terminal)

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text:
Each operation is idempotent via idempotencyKey:

  • Duplicate requests return cached result
  • No duplicate side effects
  • Safe for at-least-once delivery

docs.title: Determinism
docs.text:
Engine guarantees replay produces identical results:

  • Uses injected Clock (not Date.now())
  • Uses seeded PRNG (not Math.random())
  • Same inputs → same outputs (for correctness verification)

docs.title: Durability
docs.text:
All state transitions are atomic with outbox:

  1. Read current state
  2. Compute new state
  3. Write state + append outbox event (single transaction)
  4. Return result (outbox guarantees delivery)

docs.title: Example Implementations - IWorkflowEngineAdapter
docs.text:
• Temporal: Native Temporal workflow + activities
  • Conductor: Conductor workflow engine adaptation
  • Simple Sync: Single-threaded deterministic engine (tests)
  • Distributed: Multi-process engine with Kafka coordination

docs.title: Workflow Execution Flow
docs.text:
1. Request arrives: POST /runs

  2. Engine creates run (state: INITIALIZING)

  3. Start run: POST /runs/{id}/start

  4. Engine transitions to RUNNING

  5. Routes first step

  6. Execute step: POST /steps/{id}/execute

  7. Engine validates step is current
  8. Calls step adapter (e.g., HTTP plugin, database plugin)
  9. Stores result + event

  10. Routes next step

  11. Step completion:

  12. Event appended to outbox
  13. Projector materializes state

  14. Next step queued

  15. Terminal states:

  16. COMPLETED: All steps succeeded
  17. FAILED: Retries exhausted
  18. CANCELLED: User terminated

docs.title: State Consistency
docs.text:
State Store (current state)
    ↓
Transactional Write:
  - Update state
  - Append outbox event
    ↓
Outbox (durable queue)
    ↓
Delivery Worker (async)
    ↓
Projector (materialized views)

Result: Eventual consistency with guarantees:

  • State is durable before outbox delivery
  • Events are ordered (sequence numbers)
  • Projections eventually consistent

docs.title: For Engine Adapter
docs.text:
1. Clock: Injected via DeterminismConfig
  2. Use workflow.now() for Temporal
  3. Use injected clock for others

  4. Never use Date.now() or Date.getTime()

  5. Randomness: Injected PRNG

  6. Use seeded random for retry delays
  7. Never use Math.random()

  8. Seed must be deterministic (from event sequence)

  9. External calls: Forbidden in pure determinism

  10. Database reads: Only via state store adapter (cached)
  11. Network: Only via step adapters (external side effects)
  12. Time: Only via injected clock

docs.title: Verification (Golden Path Testing)
docs.text:
1. Record all events from production run
2. Replay run in test environment (same inputs)
3. Compare final state (golden master)
4. Assert hashes match (determinism parity)

docs.title: Priority Order (Recommended)
docs.text:
1. In-Memory: For tests (no persistence)
  2. Postgres + LocalStack: Development
  3. Temporal: Production high-volume
  4. DynamoDB: Production serverless
  5. Kafka Streams: Event-driven projection

docs.title: Contract Compliance Matrix
docs.text: Adapter Projector Engine Priority Temporal ❌ native events ✅ native 1 Postgres ✅ denormalization ✅ sagas 2 DynamoDB ✅ streams + Lambda ✅ state machine 3 Kafka ✅ stream processing ❌ not orchestration 4 In-Memory ✅ simple map ✅ state machine 0 (tests)

docs.title: Fast Path (Temporal)
docs.text:
Engine: Temporal native workflows
Projector: Temporal events → indexed views

docs.title: Scalable Path (Postgres)
docs.text:
Engine: State transitions in saga tables
Projector: Event log → materialized views

docs.title: Serverless Path (DynamoDB)
docs.text:
Engine: State stored in DynamoDB
Projector: DynamoDB Streams → Lambda → views

All use same IProjectorAdapter + IWorkflowEngineAdapter contracts.

docs.title: Next Steps (Phase 3)
docs.text:
• Implement In-Memory adapters (testing foundation)
  • Implement Postgres adapters (primary)
  • Define step execution context (for plugins)
  • Implement plugin framework

docs.text: Initial Release

docs.title: IProjectorAdapter.v1
docs.text:
• MUST transform events into queryable materialized state
  • MUST idempotently apply same event multiple times
  • MUST preserve event causality (sequence order)
  • Methods: projectEvent(), projectBatch(), queryProjectedState(), getWorkflowStateSnapshot(), rebuildProjection(), clearProjection()

docs.title: IWorkflowEngineAdapter.v1
docs.text:
• MUST orchestrate workflow execution through defined state machine
  • MUST guarantee determinism (same inputs → same outputs)
  • MUST ensure idempotency via idempotencyKey caching
  • MUST use atomic state transitions with outbox pattern
  • Methods: createRun(), startRun(), executeStep(), executeStepBatch(), pauseRun(), resumeRun(), terminateRun(), getRunState(), replayRun(), archiveRun()

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Multi-adapter support (Temporal, Postgres, DynamoDB, Kafka, In-Memory)
  • Determinism verification via golden path testing
  • Event-driven consistency model
  • Proper separation of normative contracts vs implementation details

docs.title: Contract Versioning Policy
docs.text: Audience: Architecture reviewers, SDK implementers, contract authors Stability: NORMATIVE (v1.0, patched to v1.0.1) Effective Date: February 11, 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document defines the versioning strategy for normative contracts in the DVT Workflow Engine. It establishes clear rules for when to increment major vs. minor versions, deprecation procedures, and migration paths.

docs.title: Why This Matters
docs.text:
• Stability Guarantees: Callers depend on contracts; breaking changes must be signaled clearly
  • Migration Windows: Implementations need time to adapt; we provide structured timelines
  • Backward Compatibility: Minor updates should never break existing implementations
  • Deprecation Clarity: Sunset dates prevent indefinite legacy support

docs.title: Semantic Versioning
docs.text:
All contracts follow Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 (semver):

MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
v1.0.0
↓   ↓   ↓
│   │   └─ Patch: Documentation fixes, clarifications (no normative changes)
│   └───── Minor: Backward-compatible additions
└───────── Major: Breaking changes

docs.title: Releases vs. File Series
docs.text:
• Contract files are versioned as MAJOR.MINOR series (e.g., IWorkflowEngine.v1.0.md, ExecutionSemantics.v2.0.md)
  • PATCH versions are tracked via git tags (e.g., engine/IWorkflowEngine@v1.0.1, @v1.0.2) and do not create new files
  • PATCH changes are limited to documentation fixes or clarifications that do not change normative requirements
  • Auditability: Each patch tag corresponds to a commit; revert/audit trails are clear in git history

Example:

File name (series):   IWorkflowEngine.v1.0.md
Release tags:         engine/IWorkflowEngine@v1.0.0  (initial release)
                      engine/IWorkflowEngine@v1.0.1  (doc clarification)
                      engine/IWorkflowEngine@v1.0.2  (typo fix, same semantics)

docs.title: Backward Compatibility Definition
docs.text:
A change is considered MINOR (backward compatible) only if it is backward compatible for:

  • Producers of the contract (they can continue emitting/sending old shapes without modification)
  • Consumers of the contract (they can continue accepting/handling old shapes without modification)

If either side can break without modification → the change is MAJOR.

Examples:

  • ✅ MINOR: Add optional field (producers ignore, consumers accept both old and new)
  • ❌ MAJOR: Remove field from required set (consumers might assume it exists; contract semantic changes)
  • ❌ MAJOR: Narrow enum or add pattern constraint (producers constrained tighter; silent breakage risk)
  • ❌ MAJOR: Change field semantics (even if type stays same; meaning decoupled from structure)

docs.title: 1. MINOR Update (v1.0 → v1.1)
docs.text:
✅ Allowed breaking change: NONE — minor versions are backward compatible.

Acceptable additions:

  • New optional field in JSON schema (required: [] unchanged, no default-value semantics change)
  • New optional method/procedure (existing code ignores it)
  • Clarifications and documentation improvements (no normative change)
  • Field constraint relaxation (e.g., wider valid range, relaxed pattern, expanded enum)

Explicitly BANNED (these are MAJOR):

  • Adding minLength, pattern, new enum constraints, or reducing numeric range
  • Changing default semantics or interpreting an existing field's meaning
  • Removing or renaming a field (even if optional)
  • Any change that requires producer or consumer code modification

Examples:

  • Add TimeoutPolicy as optional field to ExecutionRequest
  • Add onRetry as optional callback in WorkflowHook
  • Clarify error message wording for InvalidTransitionError

Process:

  1. Draft changes in PR with title prefix docs: (minor)
  2. Request review from contract author + 1 other maintainer
  3. Update CHANGELOG: "Minor update to IWorkflowEngine (v1.0 → v1.1)"
  4. Tag release as engine/IWorkflowEngine@v1.1.0
  5. No deprecation window needed

Backward Compatibility Guarantee:

INVARIANT: Code consuming v1.0 works unmodified with v1.1
- Old implementations ignore new optional fields
- New methods have safe defaults
- Constraints never tighten (only relax)

docs.title: 2. MAJOR Update (v1.0 → v2.0)
docs.text:
⚠️ Breaking changes allowed — requires deprecation window.

Examples of breaking changes:

  • Remove field from required set
  • Rename field or method
  • Change type of field (e.g., string → object)
  • Add new required field with no default
  • Change error code or exception type
  • Modify execution guarantee (e.g., at-least-once → at-most-once)

Examples:

  • Rename StatusUpdate → ExecutionUpdate in event schema
  • Add mandatory correlationId field to execution request
  • Change ErrorCode.TIMEOUT enum value
  • Modify retry semantics from exponential → linear backoff

Process:

Month 1 (Proposal):
├─ Author creates RFC PR
├─ Title: "refactor: (major) IWorkflowEngine v1.0 → v2.0 proposal"
├─ Includes: rationale, migration guide, examples
└─ Requires: 3+ approvals (architecture, SDK lead, ops)

Month 2 (Stabilization):
├─ v2.0-DRAFT published (`IWorkflowEngine.v2.0-DRAFT.md` in feature branch)
├─ Implementations can opt-in to testing v2.0-DRAFT
├─ Feedback integrated into v2.0 final
└─ Timeline: 4 weeks for stabilization

Month 3 (Release):
├─ v2.0 tagged as STABLE (e.g., `engine/IWorkflowEngine@v2.0.0`); v1.0 marked DEPRECATED; deprecation clock starts
├─ v1.0 tagged with deprecation notice
├─ CHANGELOG entry: "v2.0 released; v1.0 sunset: Month 6"
└─ Implementations have 3-month grace period

Month 4-6 (Sunset Window):
├─ v1.0 contract remains available ("DEPRECATED, 90-day grace period")
├─ SDK continues accepting v1.0 implementations (issues warnings)
├─ Runbooks published: "Migrating from IWorkflowEngine v1.0 to v2.0"
└─ GitHub issues labeled: #migration-path, #support-window

Month 6+ (Removal):
├─ v1.0 moved to docs/deprecated/
├─ SDK drops support for v1.0 (next major SDK release)
└─ Runbooks archived

Superseding Guarantees:

INVARIANT: v2.0 can coexist with v1.0 briefly during grace period
- SDK may accept both v1.0 and v2.0 implementations
- Adapters clearly labeled by supported version
- Runtime must NOT assume all components v2.0

docs.title: Timeline Triggers
docs.text: Start Date: When v2.0 is tagged as STABLE (release tag, e.g., engine/IWorkflowEngine@v2.0.0), not when merged to main (main continues to evolve) Duration: 90 calendar days from release tag date End Date: 90 days after release tag date
